title: How to Apply for a Marriage License in the Philippines
description: Essential legal requirements and procedures for couples planning to marry in the Philippines.

requirements.title: PSA Birth Certificate
requirements.description: Original birth certificate in security paper for both applicants.

requirements.title: PSA CENOMAR
requirements.description: Certificate of No Marriage issued by the PSA.

requirements.title: Cedula
requirements.description: Community Tax Certificate for both applicants.

requirements.title: Seminar Certificate
requirements.description: Proof of attendance from pre-marriage counseling and family planning seminars.

blocks.content: A Marriage License is an official legal document issued by the Local Government Unit (LGU) through the Local Civil Registrar (LCR), authorizing two individuals to marry in the Philippines.
Under Philippine law, most couples must obtain a marriage license before a civil or church wedding can legally proceed.

The Marriage License is commonly used for:
* Civil weddings
* Church weddings
* Legal registration of marriage

You may need a Marriage License if you are:
- Planning to get married in the Philippines
- Applying for a church or civil wedding
- Registering a legal union recognized by Philippine law

blocks.title: Legal Authority to Marry
blocks.content: The license legally authorizes a couple to marry anywhere in the Philippines within its validity period.

blocks.title: Required for Wedding Ceremonies
blocks.content: Churches, judges, mayors, and solemnizing officers usually require a valid marriage license before officiating a wedding.

blocks.title: Enables Official Marriage Registration
blocks.content: Without a valid marriage license, most marriages cannot be properly registered with the PSA.
Marriage License applications are generally processed through walk-in applications at the Local Civil Registrar (LCR) office of the city or municipality where either applicant resides.

blocks.title: Online Application
blocks.content: Some LGUs provide online appointment systems or downloadable application forms through their official websites.
However, personal appearance is usually still required for verification and seminar attendance.

blocks.title: Walk-In Application
blocks.content: Applicants may visit the Local Civil Registrar office directly to submit requirements and process their application.
Both applicants are usually required to appear in person.
**Pro Tip:** Always double-check for 'Negative Results'. If your record is missing, you must process **Late Registration** at the LCR where the event occurred.

blocks.title: Secure PSA Documents
blocks.content: Obtain updated PSA Birth Certificates and PSA CENOMAR copies for both applicants.

blocks.title: Attend Required Seminars
blocks.content:
Attend mandatory seminars such as:
* Pre-Marriage Counseling
* Family Planning Seminar
* Responsible Parenthood Seminar
Requirements vary depending on the LGU.

blocks.title: Submit Application Forms
blocks.content: Submit completed application forms along with all documentary requirements to the Local Civil Registrar.
The officer will review and verify the submitted documents.

blocks.title: Pay the Applicable Fees
blocks.content: Pay the required processing fees at the LGU cashier or authorized payment center.
Keep all official receipts.

blocks.title: Wait for the 10-Day Publication Period
blocks.content: Philippine law requires the marriage license application to be posted publicly for 10 consecutive days.
This allows any legal objections to be raised.

blocks.title: Claim the Marriage License
blocks.content: After the publication period and approval, applicants may claim their Marriage License from the Local Civil Registrar.
The license is generally valid for 120 days nationwide.

Applicants may process their Marriage License at:
- Local Civil Registrar Office (City Hall or Municipal Hall)
- LGU Civil Registry Department
- Selected LGU online appointment portals
Applications are usually filed in the city or municipality where either applicant resides.

items: [City/Municipal Hall Website](https://www.gov.ph/services/lgu) (or visit your respective local city/municipal hall)

blocks.content:
Typical processing timelines include:
* Document preparation: 1–7 days
* Seminar attendance: Same day to 2 days
* Mandatory publication period: 10 consecutive days
* License release: 10–14 days total processing

Applicants may monitor their application through:
* Local Civil Registrar inquiry desks
* LGU SMS or online appointment systems
* Phone or email follow-ups

Applicants may experience:
- Incorrect PSA records or misspelled names
- Incomplete seminar requirements
- Delayed publication period processing
- Missing parental consent documents
- Expired or invalid IDs

items: Applying too close to the wedding date
Forgetting photocopies of documents and IDs

blocks.content: Always review your application before final submission.

items: Prepare all PSA documents in advance
Book seminars early if slots are limited
Bring multiple photocopies of all documents
Apply at least 1 month before your wedding date

blocks.title: How long is a Marriage License valid?
blocks.content: A Marriage License is generally valid for 120 days from the date of issue anywhere in the Philippines.

blocks.title: Is a Marriage License required for church weddings?
blocks.content: Yes. Most churches require a valid Marriage License before conducting the ceremony.

blocks.title: Can foreigners apply for a Marriage License in the Philippines?
blocks.content: Yes, but additional requirements such as a Certificate of Legal Capacity to Marry may be required.

blocks.title: Can I apply in a different city?
blocks.content: Applications are usually filed where either applicant resides, depending on LGU rules.

blocks.title: Is the 10-day waiting period mandatory?
blocks.content: Yes. The publication period is required by Philippine law for most marriage license applications.
